questions.q:
Consider the following diseases:
1. Measles
2. Typhoid
3. Mumps
Which of the above is/are caused by a virus?
questions.e: Measles (paramyxovirus) and mumps are viral, so antibiotics do not treat them. Typhoid is caused by the bacterium Salmonella Typhi and is treatable with antibiotics.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Why Do We Fall Ill

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about antimicrobial resistance (AMR):
1. Antibiotics are effective against viral infections if taken in higher doses.
2. Bacteria can acquire resistance genes from other bacteria, for example through plasmids.
3. Stopping an antibiotic course midway can leave partly resistant bacteria alive to multiply.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Resistance spreads by horizontal gene transfer, and incomplete courses select the survivors. Antibiotics act on bacterial structures such as the cell wall or ribosome, which viruses lack, so dose does not make them work on viruses.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Human Health and Disease

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bacteria are prokaryotes.
2. Viruses can reproduce on their own outside a host cell.
3. Fungi are eukaryotes.
4. Penicillin was first obtained from the mould Penicillium.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Bacteria have no membrane-bound nucleus (prokaryotes), fungi are eukaryotes, and Fleming's penicillin came from Penicillium. Viruses are obligate parasites and can multiply only inside living host cells.
questions.s: NCERT Class 8 Science, Microorganisms: Friend and Foe

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of vitamin and deficiency disease is NOT correctly matched?
questions.e: Rickets, the softening of bones in children, is caused by lack of vitamin D (needed for calcium absorption). Thiamine deficiency causes beriberi.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Why Do We Fall Ill; Class 10 Science, Life Processes
questions.h: Thiamine = Tingling nerves = Beriberi; D = Dense bones.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Disease : Causative organism
1. Kala-azar : Leishmania (protozoan)
2. Sleeping sickness : Trypanosoma (protozoan)
3. Ringworm : Fungus
4. Diphtheria : Virus
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Kala-azar (Leishmania donovani), sleeping sickness (Trypanosoma) and ringworm (a dermatophyte fungus) are correct. Diphtheria is caused by the bacterium Corynebacterium diphtheriae, not a virus.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Why Do We Fall Ill

questions.q:
Statement-I: Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) contains glucose along with common salt.
Statement-II: Glucose in the intestine helps the absorption of sodium and thereby of water.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Sodium and glucose are absorbed together by a co-transport mechanism in the small intestine, and water follows sodium by osmosis. Hence glucose in ORS makes rehydration in diarrhoea more effective than salt alone.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Human Health and Disease

questions.q:
Statement-I: Penicillin is effective against the common cold.
Statement-II: Penicillin interferes with the synthesis of the bacterial cell wall.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Penicillin blocks cell-wall synthesis in bacteria, which is why it works on bacterial infections. The common cold is viral, and viruses have no cell wall, so Statement-I is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Human Health and Disease

questions.q:
Statement-I: Antibiotics are ineffective against influenza.
Statement-II: Influenza is caused by a bacterium that has developed resistance to antibiotics.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Influenza is caused by a virus, so antibiotics do not act on it. It is not a resistant bacterium, which makes Statement-II incorrect.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Human Health and Disease

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about nucleic acids:
1. DNA contains the sugar ribose.
2. RNA contains uracil in place of thymine.
3. In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: RNA has uracil instead of thymine, and A pairs with T (two hydrogen bonds) while G pairs with C (three) in DNA. DNA has deoxyribose, while RNA has ribose.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.q: A test cross in genetics involves crossing
o: two homozygous dominant individuals to confirm purity
an individual of unknown genotype showing the dominant trait with a homozygous recessive individual
an F1 hybrid with a homozygous dominant parent
two individuals of the F2 generation to check segregation
questions.e: A test cross with the homozygous recessive parent reveals the unknown genotype: all dominant offspring suggest a homozygous dominant parent, while a 1:1 ratio shows it was heterozygous. Mendel used it to verify his segregation results.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Heredity

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about sex determination in humans:
1. The sex of the child depends on whether the egg carries an X or a Y chromosome.
2. Human females have two X chromosomes.
3. A sperm may carry either an X or a Y chromosome.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Every egg carries an X chromosome, so the child's sex depends on the sperm: X gives a girl and Y gives a boy. The claim that the egg decides the sex is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Heredity

questions.q:
Consider the following chromosomal disorders:
1. Down syndrome is caused by an extra copy of chromosome 21.
2. Turner syndrome is a condition in females with only one X chromosome (XO).
3. Klinefelter syndrome is a condition in males with an extra X chromosome (XXY).
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three describe aneuploidy accurately: trisomy 21, monosomy X, and XXY. These arise from non-disjunction of chromosomes during gamete formation.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Principles of Inheritance and Variation

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Bt cotton expresses a gene taken from the bacterium Bacillus subtilis.
2. Golden Rice has been engineered to produce beta-carotene, a precursor of vitamin A.
3. Bt cotton is protected against attack by cotton bollworms.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Golden Rice targets vitamin A deficiency, and Bt cotton carries a cry gene that makes a protein toxic to bollworms. The gene comes from Bacillus thuringiensis (hence 'Bt'), not Bacillus subtilis.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Biotechnology and its Applications

questions.q:
With reference to CRISPR-Cas9 technology, consider the following statements:
1. Cas9 is an enzyme that cuts DNA at a site guided by a guide RNA.
2. The 2020 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded for its development.
3. CRISPR sequences were first identified in bacteria, where they form part of a defence against viruses.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: CRISPR-Cas works as an adaptive immune system of bacteria and archaea against phages, and was adapted into a gene-editing tool. Charpentier and Doudna received the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, not Physiology or Medicine.
questions.s: The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2020 (NobelPrize.org); NCERT Class 12 Biology, Biotechnology and its Applications

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about human digestion:
1. Bile is produced in the gallbladder.
2. Bile contains no digestive enzymes but helps to emulsify fats.
3. Pepsin acts on proteins in the acidic medium of the stomach.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The liver makes bile, which is only stored and concentrated in the gallbladder. Bile salts break fat globules into smaller droplets for lipase action, and HCl in gastric juice provides the acidic medium for pepsin.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Life Processes

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the human heart and blood vessels:
1. The right ventricle pumps blood into the aorta.
2. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood.
3. The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The pulmonary circuit is the exception to the rule that arteries carry oxygenated blood: the pulmonary artery takes blood to the lungs, and the pulmonary vein returns it. The right ventricle feeds the pulmonary artery, while the left ventricle pumps into the aorta.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Life Processes
questions.h: Pulmonary = the odd one out: artery blue, vein red.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Erythroblastosis foetalis due to Rh incompatibility usually affects the second Rh-positive child of an Rh-negative mother rather than the first.
Statement-II: An Rh-negative mother produces anti-Rh antibodies after foetal Rh-positive blood enters her circulation at the first delivery.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: At the first delivery, foetal Rh-positive cells mix with maternal blood and sensitise the mother, who forms anti-Rh antibodies. In a later pregnancy these antibodies cross the placenta and destroy foetal red cells.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Human Reproduction / Principles of Inheritance

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Excess secretion of growth hormone in adults causes gigantism.
2. Deficiency of iodine causes goitre.
3. Deficiency of insulin causes diabetes mellitus.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Iodine is needed for thyroxine; its lack enlarges the thyroid, and insulin lack raises blood glucose. Excess growth hormone in children causes gigantism, while in adults it causes acromegaly.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Control and Coordination

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The medulla oblongata controls involuntary actions such as breathing and heartbeat.
2. The cerebellum helps maintain posture and balance.
3. The hypothalamus helps regulate body temperature, hunger and thirst.
4. Reflex actions such as withdrawing the hand from a hot object are controlled by the cerebrum.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 to 3 are correct. A simple reflex is mediated through the spinal cord (reflex arc) without waiting for the cerebrum, which is why the hand is pulled away before the pain is registered.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Control and Coordination

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly identifies the site of ultrafiltration of blood in the nephron?
questions.e: Blood is filtered under pressure through the glomerular capillaries into Bowman's capsule. The later parts of the nephron only reabsorb useful substances or secrete wastes.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Life Processes

questions.q: Carbon monoxide poisoning is dangerous mainly because carbon monoxide
o: destroys red blood cells by dissolving their membrane
blocks the entry of air into the nostrils
prevents the heart from pumping blood to the lungs
binds to haemoglobin with much greater affinity than oxygen, reducing oxygen transport
questions.e: CO forms carboxyhaemoglobin, which is very stable, so haemoglobin cannot carry oxygen to tissues. It does not obstruct the airway or rupture red cells.
questions.s: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Breathing and Exchange of Gases

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about malnutrition:
1. Kwashiorkor is characterised by severe wasting without any oedema.
2. Marasmus is characterised by severe wasting due to deficiency of both calories and protein.
3. Kwashiorkor is characterised by swelling (oedema) due to protein deficiency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Marasmus is wasting from overall energy and protein shortage. Kwashiorkor, from protein deficiency, shows oedema, a swollen belly and thin hair, so wasting without oedema describes marasmus, not kwashiorkor.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Why Do We Fall Ill; Economic Survey (nutrition)

questions.q:
With reference to food fortification in India, consider the following statements:
1. Fortified rice kernels are blended with ordinary rice to provide iron, folic acid and vitamin B12.
2. Double fortified salt contains iodine and vitamin D.
3. The '+F' logo is used by FSSAI to identify fortified foods.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Fortified rice delivers iron, folic acid and B12 against anaemia, and FSSAI marks fortified foods with the '+F' logo. Double fortified salt is fortified with iodine and iron, not vitamin D.
questions.s: FSSAI; PIB (Ministry of Consumer Affairs)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about polio:
1. The Salk vaccine is the oral polio vaccine.
2. India was certified polio-free by the World Health Organization in 2014.
3. Oral polio vaccine uses live attenuated virus, while the injectable vaccine uses inactivated virus.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The WHO South-East Asia Region, including India, was certified polio-free on 27 March 2014. Salk's vaccine is the injectable inactivated one (IPV), while Sabin's is the oral vaccine (OPV).
questions.s: PIB / WHO, 27 Mar 2014; NCERT Class 12 Biology, Human Health and Disease

questions.q:
Match List-I (Vaccine) with List-II (Type of platform) and select the correct answer using the code below:
List-I
A. Covishield (Oxford-AstraZeneca)
B. Covaxin
C. ZyCoV-D
D. Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine
List-II
1. mRNA
2. Inactivated whole virus
3. Viral vector
4. DNA plasmid
questions.e: Covishield uses a chimpanzee adenovirus vector, Covaxin is an inactivated whole-virion vaccine, ZyCoV-D is a DNA plasmid vaccine and Pfizer-BioNTech is an mRNA vaccine.
questions.s: PIB / ICMR; NCERT Class 12 Biology, Human Health and Disease

questions.q: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) is defined as TB caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis that is resistant to at least
questions.e: Isoniazid and rifampicin are the two most powerful first-line anti-TB drugs, so resistance to both defines MDR-TB. Such patients need longer, costlier second-line regimens.
questions.s: WHO Global TB Programme; Park's / NCERT Class 12 Biology

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Disease : Vector
1. Dengue : Aedes aegypti mosquito
2. Japanese encephalitis : Culex mosquito
3. Kala-azar : Tsetse fly
4. Lymphatic filariasis : Culex mosquito
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Dengue (Aedes), Japanese encephalitis (Culex) and filariasis (Culex quinquefasciatus carrying Wuchereria) are correct. Kala-azar is spread by the sandfly, while tsetse flies spread sleeping sickness.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Human Health and Disease

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about viral hepatitis:
1. A widely used vaccine against hepatitis C is available.
2. Hepatitis A and E spread mainly through contaminated food and water.
3. Hepatitis B spreads through infected blood and body fluids, and a vaccine is available against it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A and E are faecal-oral (water-borne), while B and C are blood-borne. Hepatitis C has no vaccine, though modern antivirals can cure it.
questions.s: WHO fact sheets on hepatitis; NCERT Class 12 Biology

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about HIV:
1. HIV can spread through the bite of a mosquito that has fed on an infected person.
2. HIV mainly infects the helper T (CD4) cells of the immune system.
3. The genetic material of HIV is RNA, which is copied into DNA by reverse transcriptase.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: HIV is a retrovirus: it uses reverse transcriptase to make DNA that integrates into the host genome, and it weakens immunity by depleting CD4 cells. It is not spread by mosquito bites, because it does not multiply in insects.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Human Health and Disease

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the history of vaccination and disease eradication:
1. Smallpox is the first human disease declared eradicated worldwide.
2. Polio has been declared eradicated worldwide.
3. Edward Jenner used material from cowpox lesions to protect against smallpox.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: WHO declared smallpox eradicated in 1980, after Jenner's 1796 cowpox-based method led to mass vaccination. Polio has not been eradicated globally: wild poliovirus still circulates in a few countries.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Human Health and Disease; WHO

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Disease : Year India was certified free of it by the WHO
1. Polio : 2014
2. Maternal and neonatal tetanus : 2015
3. Yaws : 2016
4. Smallpox : 1990
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: India was certified polio-free in 2014, free of maternal and neonatal tetanus in 2015, and free of yaws in 2016. Smallpox was certified eradicated in 1977 (the last case in India was in 1975), not 1990.
questions.s: PIB / WHO releases; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about sickle cell anaemia:
1. It is an inherited autosomal recessive disorder.
2. It is caused by a virus that infects red blood cells.
3. It results from a single amino acid substitution in the beta chain of haemoglobin.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A point mutation replaces glutamic acid with valine in the beta globin chain, making red cells sickle-shaped when oxygen is low. A person needs two defective copies to be affected, and it is genetic, not infectious.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Principles of Inheritance and Variation; Ministry of Health

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A prion is an infectious protein particle without nucleic acid.
2. A virus can contain both DNA and RNA as genetic material simultaneously.
3. A viroid is a small naked infectious RNA without a protein coat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Prions cause diseases such as mad cow disease (BSE), and viroids infect plants. A virus carries only one kind of nucleic acid, either DNA or RNA, never both.
questions.s: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Biological Classification

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about probiotics and gut microbes:
1. Probiotics are live microorganisms that give a health benefit when consumed in adequate amounts.
2. Prebiotics are non-digestible food components that nourish beneficial gut bacteria.
3. Gut bacteria can synthesise some vitamins, including vitamin K.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are accurate: curd bacteria are a familiar probiotic, dietary fibre is a prebiotic, and intestinal flora produce vitamin K and some B vitamins that supplement the diet.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Microbes in Human Welfare

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Product : Microbe involved
1. Curd : Lactobacillus
2. Bread dough rising : Saccharomyces cerevisiae
3. Large holes in Swiss cheese : Propionibacterium sharmanii
4. Streptomycin : Aspergillus niger
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Lactic acid bacteria set milk into curd, baker's yeast releases CO2 that raises dough, and CO2 from Propionibacterium makes the cheese holes. Streptomycin is obtained from the bacterium Streptomyces, while Aspergillus niger is used for citric acid.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Microbes in Human Welfare

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about biofertilisers:
1. Rhizobium forms symbiotic root nodules in leguminous plants and fixes atmospheric nitrogen.
2. Mycorrhizal fungi help plants chiefly by fixing atmospheric nitrogen.
3. Azotobacter is a free-living nitrogen-fixing bacterium.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Mycorrhiza is a fungus-root association that mainly improves uptake of phosphorus and water, not nitrogen fixation. Rhizobium (symbiotic) and Azotobacter (free-living) are true nitrogen fixers.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Microbes in Human Welfare

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Methanogens produce methane during anaerobic breakdown of organic waste in biogas plants.
2. A higher Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) of water indicates lower organic pollution.
3. Secondary treatment of sewage relies on aerobic microbes to reduce BOD.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Biogas is mostly methane from methanogens, and secondary treatment uses aerated flocs of bacteria to consume organic matter. High BOD means much organic matter and therefore heavier pollution.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Microbes in Human Welfare

questions.q:
Match List-I (Type of cancer) with List-II (Tissue of origin):
List-I
A. Carcinoma
B. Sarcoma
C. Leukaemia
D. Lymphoma
List-II
1. Blood-forming tissue with uncontrolled increase of white cells
2. Lymphoid tissue
3. Epithelial tissue
4. Connective or muscle tissue
questions.e: Carcinomas arise in epithelial lining (most common cancers), sarcomas in bone, cartilage or muscle, leukaemia in the bone marrow and blood, and lymphoma in lymph nodes.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Human Health and Disease

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about dietary fats and cholesterol:
1. HDL helps to carry cholesterol away from tissues to the liver.
2. Trans fats raise HDL and lower LDL.
3. LDL contributes to the deposit of cholesterol in artery walls.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: HDL is 'good' cholesterol and LDL is 'bad' cholesterol that forms plaques in arteries. Trans fats do the opposite of the claim made: they raise LDL and lower HDL, raising the risk of heart disease.
questions.s: NCERT Class 11 Biology; FSSAI nutrition material

questions.q:
With reference to the Anaemia Mukt Bharat strategy, consider the following statements:
1. It follows a 6x6x6 strategy of six beneficiary groups, six interventions and six institutional mechanisms.
2. Iron and folic acid supplementation is one of its interventions.
3. It focuses exclusively on pregnant women.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Anaemia Mukt Bharat, launched in 2018, covers children, adolescents, women of reproductive age and pregnant and lactating women. It is not limited to pregnant women.
questions.s: PIB, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare; Economic Survey

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about human blood groups:
1. A person with blood group AB has neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies in the plasma.
2. Red cells of blood group O carry neither A nor B antigens.
3. A person with blood group O can safely receive red cells from a person of group A.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Group O red cells lack A and B antigens, so O is the universal red-cell donor; group AB plasma lacks both antibodies, so AB is the universal recipient. A group O person has anti-A and anti-B antibodies, which would destroy group A cells.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Principles of Inheritance and Variation

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about human genome and DNA technology:
1. The Human Genome Project determined the sequence of roughly three billion base pairs of human DNA.
2. Taq polymerase used in PCR is derived from a heat-tolerant bacterium, Thermus aquaticus.
3. DNA fingerprinting was developed by Kary Mullis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Heat-stable Taq polymerase survives the repeated 95 degree Celsius denaturation steps of PCR. DNA fingerprinting, based on variable repeat sequences, was developed by Alec Jeffreys, whereas Kary Mullis invented PCR.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Biotechnology: Principles and Processes

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Nipah virus:
1. It is a zoonotic virus.
2. Fruit bats of the genus Pteropus are its natural reservoir.
3. It is transmitted exclusively by the Aedes mosquito.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Nipah spreads from fruit bats to humans directly or through contaminated fruit or infected animals such as pigs, and then between people by close contact. Mosquitoes are not its vector, so the Aedes claim is wrong.
questions.s: WHO fact sheet on Nipah; Ministry of Health

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of a hormone and the gland producing it is NOT correctly matched?
o: Insulin : Beta cells of the pancreas
Glucagon : Beta cells of the pancreas
questions.e: Glucagon comes from the alpha cells of the islets of Langerhans, and insulin from the beta cells, and they act oppositely on blood sugar. Adrenaline comes from the adrenal medulla, and melatonin, which regulates sleep rhythm, from the pineal gland.
questions.s: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chemical Coordination and Integration
questions.h: Alpha = Add glucose (glucagon); Beta = Bring it down.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Rods in the retina are responsible for vision in dim light.
2. Cones are responsible for colour vision and vision in bright light.
3. Cataract is the clouding of the eye lens.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Rods contain rhodopsin, which needs vitamin A, so night blindness results from its lack, while cones give colour vision. Cataract clouds the lens and is treated by replacing it with an artificial intraocular lens.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Human Eye and the Colourful World; Class 11 Biology

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the human immune system:
1. Antibodies are produced by plasma cells derived from B lymphocytes.
2. T lymphocytes mature in the thymus.
3. B lymphocytes are mainly responsible for cell-mediated immunity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: B cells give humoral (antibody) immunity, and T cells give cell-mediated immunity. The 'T' stands for thymus, where these cells mature, while B cells mature in bone marrow.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Human Health and Disease

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The hormone hCG is detected in urine in common pregnancy test kits.
2. Fertilisation in humans normally occurs in the fallopian tube.
3. Sex determination of the foetus through amniocentesis is legally prohibited in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: hCG is produced by the placenta after implantation, and fertilisation occurs in the ampullary region of the fallopian tube. The PC&PNDT Act 1994 bans prenatal sex determination, although amniocentesis is allowed to detect genetic disorders.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Reproductive Health; PC&PNDT Act, 1994

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly describes recombinant human insulin production?
o: Insulin is extracted from human blood donors and purified
Insulin is synthesised by growing human pancreas cells in sheep
The human insulin gene is introduced into bacteria such as Escherichia coli, which then produce the hormone
Bacteria are fed glucose so that they secrete natural insulin on their own
questions.e: Recombinant DNA technology inserted the human insulin genes into E. coli, giving the first recombinant drug (Humulin) and ending dependence on animal pancreas extract. Bacteria do not make insulin unless they carry the human gene.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Biotechnology and its Applications

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about cloning and stem cells:
1. Dolly the sheep was produced by transferring the nucleus of a somatic cell into an enucleated egg.
2. Induced pluripotent stem cells are made by reprogramming adult cells.
3. Embryonic stem cells can give rise to only one type of cell.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Dolly was cloned by somatic cell nuclear transfer, and Yamanaka showed that adult cells can be reprogrammed into pluripotent stem cells. Embryonic stem cells are pluripotent, so they can give rise to many cell types, not just one.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Biotechnology and its Applications

questions.q: The vaccine against human papillomavirus (HPV) is mainly intended to prevent
questions.e: Persistent infection with high-risk HPV types such as 16 and 18 causes most cervical cancers. Liver cancer is linked to hepatitis B and C viruses.
questions.s: WHO fact sheet on cervical cancer; Ministry of Health
